findings.claim: No reviewed record names Michael Glasgow’s parents. Robert Glasgow-1512 is retained as a selected uncertain working father at 23%, not as proved parentage.
findings.reasoning: The July instruction not to attach Robert was superseded by the qualified working selection of 16 October 2026. The current father assessment remains 23%: the Ayr Robert/Margaret Donald household and the Irvine Michael household have no parent-identifying bridge. The 1679 summons records an adult skinner; it is not Michael’s birth event. The separate 43% Margaret Donald mother hypothesis recorded on 6 November must not be treated as proof that Robert is Michael’s known father or that Michael was born in 1679.

findings.claim: An Irvine councillor named Michael Glasgow was in office by 16 April 1686 and served as a trades councillor in September 1702.
findings.reasoning: The printed burgh muniments directly name him on those dates. Identity with the subject is strong but indirect because the entries do not call him a saddler. The profile says 'before 1680,' which is compatible with the civic record; no exact birth year can be inferred.

findings.claim: Surviving Irvine civic and trades records are the best remaining route to a parent-identifying record.
findings.reasoning: The burgh catalogue lists council indexes and minutes, a Dean of Guild register, and an Incorporated Trades minute book spanning Michael's career. Burgess, apprentice, or craft admissions sometimes state a father or master, but these records have not been inspected.

objective: Resolve Michael Glasgow’s duplicate documentary household accounts, then test his uncertain Ayrshire parentage using a discriminating original record; preserve the distinction between adult occurrence and birth date.

questions.answer: On 11 November 2026 the documentary Michael/Katharine Baird accounts record-ancestry-glasgow-f6955358d5e4 and record-ancestry-glasgow-17b6fc36789d were merged reversibly into Glasgow-1406. The named parents, dates and already identified Elizabeth-1409/Janet-1407 child entries establish one documentary household. Their duplicated 12% Robert-father hypotheses are retained as historical, not current selections. The earlier 1679 skinner/later saddler identification remains the existing locality/trade inference; no new original inspection or parent proof.
questions.question: Which records prove the subject's identity across events?

questions.answer: Unresolved. Robert Glasgow-1512 remains the selected working father at 23%, with no newly inspected father clause. Margaret Donald-1722 has a separate 43% mother hypothesis, not a record-proved maternity; its reasoning uses 1679 as a birth year although that is an adult summons date. Preserve the hypotheses and their histories while checking those premises. Duplicate Michael/Katharine household accounts were reconciled on 11 November 2026. Next inspect the actual Irvine admission/guild or trades text for a father, master, residence or property bridge. Relevant archive references are Gr1/7/1, Gr1/5/1, Gr1/1/5-6 (NRS B37/12/4-5), and Gr1/23/3. Published council appearances and catalogue descriptions have already been checked and do not name a parent.
questions.question: Which original or indexed records identify the parents?

questions.answer: The indexed 9 June 1703 Kilmarnock marriage names Michael Glasgow and Katharin Baird. The known Irvine Baird child group includes Elizabeth-1409 (12 November 1710) and Janet-1407 (30 January 1715); the duplicate documentary fathers have been consolidated into Glasgow-1406. Keep the earlier Elizabeth Garven household distinct. Original parish images remain uninspected; child and parent index rows for the same event are not independent witnesses.

questions.answer: The profile's 'before 1680' date is compatible with a same-name Irvine councillor already in office in 1686; the unresolved issue is whether that councillor was the saddler. A separate Michael Glasgow found in a 1559-60 Stevenston teind list is more than a century too early and is excluded.

web_searches.purpose: Find contemporary or transcribed Irvine records that establish Michael's age, occupation, or family before 1700.
web_searches.result_summary: The published Irvine muniments name Michael Glasgow as a councillor on 16 April 1686 and again in September 1702, when he was selected among the trades councillors. They name no relative.

web_searches.purpose: Identify surviving original Irvine records most likely to contain a burgess, apprentice, or craft relationship.
web_searches.query: Irvine Burgh catalogue Dean of Guild Incorporated Trades council minutes 1680 1700
web_searches.result_summary: A Wayback capture of the North Ayrshire catalogue identifies Gr1/7/1, Gr1/5/1, Gr1/1/5-6, and Gr1/23/3. They are not publicly digitised in the reviewed catalogue.

web_searches.purpose: Separate earlier same-name Scots from the Irvine saddler.
web_searches.result_summary: A Michael Glasgow in a Stevenston teind list belongs to 1559-60 and is excluded as the subject or a plausible father. No parent-identifying probate or relational record was found online.
